items.doc: Offer the meta-agent$* commands, so the model can define an agent. Off by default: they cost ~710 tokens of prompt that most sessions never use.
The agents dispatched above this turn (set by a dispatch).
How many agents deep this turn is (set by a dispatch).
The instance this turn IS, when it is a subagent (set by a dispatch).
Replaces the ReAct instruction block for a subagent's turn.

Work tier → "provider/model" label. Ships all-nil: :standard and :deep are inert until configured, and an unset :light runs side tasks (recap, command rephrasing) on the session provider's light model.
Who dispatched this subagent turn: another instance's id, or "root" (set by a dispatch; recorded in its trajectory, byj-gly.298.1).
Directories to load agents from, replacing the defaults (project, ~/.brainyard).
Agent name → {:default :min :max} work tier, over what the agent declares.

items.whyNot: :allowed-dirs is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: Directories a tool may read and write, beyond the working dir. Unset means /tmp, the system temp dir, the working dir and ~/.brainyard. The system temp dir is $TMPDIR — on macOS a per-user /var/folders/…/T/, where programs put temporary files rather than /tmp.
Listen at <session-dir>/ask.sock (0600) so another session or a script can ask this one something; a request becomes a turn when the session is waiting for input.
The longest a request over the session channel waits for its turn to end; a request that times out still runs.

What the full-screen renderer writes to the terminal when a session turns to Needs input (a permission ask opens), once per ask: bell (BEL, which a terminal or tmux marks on a background tab or window), osc9 (a desktop notification naming the session — iTerm2, WezTerm, kitty, Ghostty, Windows Terminal), both, or off (byj-gly.328).
Total time a call may run before the model is handed a marker. Past :fast-eval-timeout-ms it is already a task; this is when the caller stops waiting for it.

items.whyNot: :auto-mode-classifier-lm is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: The model the auto-mode classifier asks, as provider/model. Sonnet: measured faster than haiku through claude -p (median 5.3 s against 8.0 s), the same cost per verdict, fewer needless prompts (byj-gly.285.3).

items.whyNot: :auto-mode-classifier? is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: In :auto outside a container, where a gate would ask, a classifier (predictor permission/classify) decides first: allow runs the call, block refuses it with a reason, unsure asks. Off: :auto asks, as brainyard's does.

items.whyNot: :auto-mode-classify-every-command? is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: In :auto, classify every command a tool runs, not only those :bash-ask-commands names — measured: the list missed every dangerous command it does not name (python -c, : > file, curl | sh, npm publish), the classifier none (byj-gly.285.3). Costs a classifier call per new command line in a request. Off: only the list's commands.

items.whyNot: :auto-mode-on-unsure is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: What :auto does when the classifier is unsure or fails: :ask the person (headless: refuse), or :deny.
Polls of one still-running task tolerated in a turn before it is parked. The first is always allowed.

items.whyNot: :bash-allow-commands is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: Programs a command line may run, as globs. Empty means anything. Not a sandbox: a line that cannot be segmented is refused.

items.whyNot: :bash-ask-commands is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: Command shapes that could destroy or change things, as globs over one command of a line (its words, past VAR=value): a matching command is asked about even inside the allowed directories — in :auto, the classifier decides (byj-gly.285.4). [] asks about none.

items.whyNot: :bash-deny-commands is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: Globs refused anywhere in a command line, whatever the mode.
The PATH /drive looks bd up on; the process's PATH when unset. A test points it at a stand-in.
Include the agent roster shipped in resources.

items.whyNot: :builtin-hooks? installs the permission gates; turning it off from inside a turn would disarm them for every later run. Edit the file by hand.
items.doc: Install the built-in hooks, including the loop guard and the permission gates.
Include the skills shipped in resources, last in precedence: a project or user skill of the same name shadows one (RFC-017).
Cache lifetime for the marked zones: 5m, or 1h (a 2x write premium).
How long after its last turn or rewind a session keeps its own newest :changes-turns turn refs (RFC-069, byj-ayk); past it, only what the repository's newest :changes-turns hold.

How many turn refs (:changes?) are kept: the repository's newest, by commit time, across its sessions, and besides them each session's own newest while it was used within :changes-days, so a long session keeps its first turns however many other sessions run. An older one is deleted as a turn ends, and git's gc takes what only it held; a rewind's refs are kept alike. A turn that changed nothing shares its trees with the turn before, so its ref costs a commit object (RFC-069).

Keep each turn's change as git keeps things: the project's work tree snapshotted as the turn begins and ends (commit objects, through an index of byj's own: HEAD, the index, the stash and the work tree untouched), every turn kept as refs/byj/turns/<session>/<turn> whose parent is its start — what a write-file, a bash command or a tangle changed alike. byj turns lists and diffs them, byj-review shows one in magit or vc (RFC-069). Nothing outside a git work tree.

The project's own check — its test or build command, run with sh -c in a task's tree — that a loop's task set takes as its machine check when it is built with no --check or --plan and holds none (RFC-071, byj-ng7.9).
More commands a delegated Claude Code session may run without asking, as Claude Code permission rules — the project's test command, say: ["Bash(python3 -m unittest:*)"] (byj-gly.292, RFC-039).
Allow a delegated session the shipped read-only and local commands (resources/brainyard/claude/allow.edn). Off: only :claude-allow.

Let a delegated Claude Code session add its own attribution to commits and pull requests (a Co-Authored-By trailer, a generated-with line). Off: its settings hide it (claude-agent/no-attribution, byj-gly.308), unless :claude-settings sets attribution itself.
The beads CLI a delegation's outcome is noted on its bead with (claude$finish).
The Claude Code CLI the agent page starts and resumes Claude Code sessions with (byj-gly.287.3, RFC-033).
The GitHub CLI claude$handoff finds a delegation's pull request with, and names in the command that opens it.
The remote a finished delegation's branch is pushed to: in the commands claude$handoff gives its caller, and the remote-tracking ref it checks when the session published (RFC-039, byj-gly.307).
How long session$send waits for a live Claude Code session to take a task handed to it and answer — idle first, then its turn (byj-gly.429). session$ask waits :ask-timeout-ms.
Where Claude Code keeps its sessions; ~/.claude when unset. A test points it at a fixture.
What a delegation to Claude Code may cost, priced from its transcript, before agent$claude stops guiding it and asks.
How many of a Claude Code session's turns agent$claude watches and guides before it reports back (RFC-039).
The model a Claude Code session agent$claude starts is given when its plan names none (claude/plan's :model), e.g. "sonnet". Unset: Claude Code's own default, which is the account's (byj-gly.320).

The --permission-mode agent$claude starts a Claude Code session with (RFC-039). auto, so its classifier passes routine commands that acceptEdits sent to the person one dialog at a time (byj-gly.290.9); pushing stays out of the session either way, by its deny rules and publish guard, unless the task tells it to publish (byj-gly.307).
A --settings file or JSON agent$claude starts a Claude Code session with, e.g. one that sets byj's gates as its PreToolUse hook (byj hook claude-settings, RFC-012).
How long a Claude Code session agent$claude waits on must stay idle before its turn counts as over.
Register the claude$* commands, which drive Claude Code sessions (RFC-039). agent$claude's own config turns them on for its turn; off elsewhere, so no other turn pays for them.
How long agent$claude waits for one turn of a Claude Code session before it reports it still running.

Whether /usage and the status line show the Claude Code subscription's windows (session, weekly, per model), read from Claude Code's own OAuth token, read-only, at api.anthropic.com/api/oauth/usage — not a public interface, so any failure reads as unknown (byj-gly.324). auto: when the session runs on the claude-code provider; on; off. /doctor shows them whatever this says.

The session's agent can coach the person toward a goal (/emacs coach, RFC-067): coach$set keeps the goal in the session's directory, and while it is set every turn is told it and how to coach — they write the code, the agent hints by degrees and checks. Never a subagent's.
The Codex CLI the agent page starts and resumes Codex sessions with (byj-gly.430.4, RFC-049).
How long session$send waits for a live Codex session to take a task handed to it and answer — idle first, then its turn (byj-gly.430.5).
Where Codex keeps its state; $CODEX_HOME, else ~/.codex, when unset (RFC-049). A test points it at a fixture.
What one agent$codex delegation may spend, priced from prices.edn's :openai rates, before it stops to ask a person; a model the table does not price is never over (byj-gly.430.7).
How many of a Codex session's turns agent$codex waits out and judges before it stops (byj-gly.430.6).
The model agent$codex starts a Codex session with when its plan names none; Codex's own default when unset.

Refuse to delegate to Codex (agent$codex) where Codex's own sandbox cannot start — Linux without unprivileged user namespaces, a container such as a Share machine — rather than run the session unsandboxed with the publish guard alone between it and a push, which it does by default and says (RFC-049 decision 7, byj-1wv.62.12).
How long a Codex session agent$codex waits on must stay idle before its turn counts as over.
Register the codex$* commands, which drive Codex sessions (RFC-049). agent$codex's own config turns them on for its turn; off elsewhere.
How long agent$codex waits for one of a Codex session's turns to end.

A slash command a file defines (/init, /share WORDS, .brainyard/commands/) becomes a turn whose request is rephrased for this session's agent in the light of the turns so far (the session/rephrase-command predictor); off, its fixed template is used. With no turns yet the template is used either way.
Directories to load the slash commands that stand for an agent from, replacing the defaults (.brainyard/commands in the project, ~/.brainyard/commands).
Render the bound tools as one line each, with get-tool-info for arguments. Ignored when :tool-discovery? is false.
In the compact tool listing, a user tool's line carries its arguments (byj-gly.251).

Tier 2 (RFC-014): when eliding is not enough, summarize the iterations older than the verbatim floor into one record (the react/compact predictor) before dropping any. A model call, made only where records would otherwise be dropped.
Composing Tools names the project's user tools, with their arguments, as the thing to call before writing a tool$run body (byj-gly.251).
Offer config$set/unset/revert — changing settings from inside a turn. Permission keys are never writable either way (RFC-013).
How many direct calls the next turn is told about, newest kept.
How long each direct call's line and result may be, as the next turn reads it.
Margin held back, since tokens are estimated as chars/4.

The model a run asks unless -p/-m say otherwise, as provider/model (e.g. claude-code/haiku, anthropic/claude-sonnet-5, openai/gpt-4.1-mini). Sonnet through the Claude Code CLI unless set (byj-gly.366; haiku before). An API key in the environment does not choose it.

items.whyNot: :denied-paths is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: Files and directories no path tool reads or writes, in any mode, nor names a directory holding: a person's logins and keys (byj-1wv.115.40), the connections the agent builder keeps among them (byj-1wv.115.44). ~ is the home. A shell's arguments are not paths the gate sees.

How many turns one bead gets in a /drive run: one judged unfinished after its last is set aside for the person — its claim released, labelled human, which /drive passes over — and the run goes on to the next ready bead (RFC-073, byj-dw0).
How many steps — a bead's turn, or a retry of one — one /drive run takes at most, whatever the profile's own limits (RFC-073).
Register the drive$* commands, which /drive's loop works a project's goal with (RFC-073). agent$drive's own config turns them on for its turn; off elsewhere.
Elide a file read whose path a later read supersedes.
The longest emacs$org-execute waits for a block to run in the person's Emacs (RFC-067). Emacs waits while it runs, and stopping at the bound does not stop it there.

Which Emacs byj reaches — the tools, @here, a clicked file, the revert after the agent's tools (RFC-067): "project", the project's own daemon that the Terminal view's emacs starts (byj-<tag>); or a server name or socket path, as emacsclient -s takes — "server" is your own Emacs's default server (M-x server-start). Yours is never reached unless named here.

The session's agent works with Emacs (RFC-067, byj-gly.459): emacs$status where emacsclient is, and while the Emacs :emacs-server names is up emacs$context, emacs$read (a buffer as Emacs has it, unsaved edits included), emacs$show, emacs$eval, emacs$note (notes on lines, listed for next-error), emacs$edit (a change in a buffer, one undo step, unsaved) and the org tools emacs$org-outline, emacs$org-tangle and emacs$org-execute. emacs$eval and emacs$org-execute run code as the person, so :tool-ask-effects asks before them by default (:editor/eval, :editor/execute). Never a subagent's.
Tell the next turn about each tool you call directly (`:<tool> …`): the line and the start of its result, so the model knows what you just looked at (brainyard's console activity).
Measure the prompt and compact the history when it exceeds the budget.
Offer the model's suggested next question (next-user-prompt) in the empty input line; → takes it.
Mouse reporting in the full-screen renderer: the wheel scrolls and a click opens a fold or a subagent. Off keeps the terminal's own click-drag text selection.
After successful multi-step turns, have a model propose a new skill from what the agent did; proposals are staged under .brainyard/skills/proposals for a person to accept.
When a turn that loaded a skill fails, or a skill that runs itself fails, have a model judge whether the SKILL.md was at fault and stage a revision.
Kill switch for agent-to-agent invocation: no agent$* tool is registered.

When a tool$run body repeats or composes tools in turns that answered, have a model generalise it into a user tool, prove it by replaying what it did, and stage it at /proposals for a person to accept.
Kill-switch for firing user hooks; the files stay on disk.
Rotated event logs kept beside the live one.

Rotate the event log past this size. 50 MiB rather than 10 because the records are now whole prompts and replies — at the old limit a day of real work would roll the log, and with it anything derived from it.

Append every event to <project>/.brainyard/logs/events.log — the one record of what happened, written whole: no payload trimmed, no string clipped, so a dataset can be derived from it (RFC-026, RFC-021). Only :agent.llm/chunk is left out, being a second copy of a reply already recorded.
How long a tool call may run inline before it becomes a background task. 0 disables detaching.
Offer flow$check — report every problem with a behavior-tree loop without running it.
Newest N turns keep their full tool trail; older ones are summarised.
Tool-name globs hidden from a turn, and from every turn below it.
Offer the hook$* commands.
Register the init$* commands, which check and prepare a project for brainyard (RFC-040). agent$init's own config turns them on for its turn; off elsewhere.
Records of finished one-shot runs kept under .brainyard/sessions — bounded by count alone, since a run that ended cannot be resumed and the TTL is what lets them pile up (RFC-016).

The full-screen renderer keeps its rails across restarts, per project, in .brainyard/rails.edn: each rail's open or closed, its view and width, and what its sections fold (byj-gly.457). Never in a run that saves no session (:persist-session? false).
Most recent sessions always kept, whatever their age.
Most recent iteration records never elided or dropped.

Refuse write-file and update-file on a file org-babel tangled with link comments (:comments link), naming the org file to edit instead: in a literate project the org file is the source (RFC-067, the tangled-file-guard hook). Off, such a file is written like any other, and the next tangle overwrites it.
Max nesting depth for subagent (agent-call) recursion.
Cap on a remembered turn's answer.
How many refusals a turn may have before a check attached to the ReAct loop's answer-check slot no longer refuses its answer (RFC-072). Every refusal counts, the answer gate's too.
The model's context window, for the prompt budget.
Iteration records kept in the prompt.
Iteration ceiling for one turn.
Agents named in the prompt.
Skills named in the prompt; the rest are found with skills$find.
Cap on a tool result in the prompt.
Room reserved for the reply when budgeting.
Turns of history the session keeps (by run).
Cap on a remembered turn's question.
How many times a turn may have its answer refused and try again. 0 disables the gate entirely.
Consecutive provider failures before the turn aborts.
Consecutive no-action replies before the turn aborts.
Live subagent instances; at the cap, the least recently asked idle one is evicted.
Cap on a task's captured output.
The most members a team runs at once. Each costs model turns of its own.
Cap on a recorded reasoning field.
Tool calls dispatched per iteration.
Turns a session will run before it stops.
Turns one session may park on a task.
The MCP Registry /mcp find searches — the official one, or a mirror or subregistry speaking its API.
Let /mcp find also search the MCP Registry (network); what it lists is third-party code, so /mcp add adds one from there disabled.

MCP servers to start, {name {:command :args :env :enabled}}; :only-named? true offers a server's tools only to an agent whose :tools names them. stdio only; a remote server is reachable through `npx -y mcp-remote <url>`. Merged per server across the config files: a project entry changes only what it names, e.g. {"github" {:enabled false}}.
How long a turn's start waits for an MCP server still starting when a user tool calls one of its tools; past it, the turn goes on without that user tool.
Offer mcp$servers when any MCP server is connected.
Command that deletes one memory for /memory: it is given the key (byj-gly.327).

Tell each turn which of the project's memories its question is about: their keys and first lines, matched on words with no model call, in the turn's own section of the prompt — never their contents, which stay memory$read's. The thresholds are the session tree's :session/memory-hint node (byj-gly.335, RFC-042).
Command that lists every memory for /memory, printing JSON: an object of key to content, or an array of {key, value} (byj-gly.327).
Cap on what a memory command returns to the model.
Command that reads one memory: it is given the key.
Command that searches memory: it is given the query.
Cap on the memory half of `search`.
Command that writes a memory: it is given the content.
Deadline for a memory command.
Offer memory$* when the store's command is on PATH. Nothing is ever injected into the prompt.
Tool results smaller than this are left alone: the stub would cost as much.

How much of a turn is shown: default (the answer and the tools it called), concise (the answer, no tool block), explanatory (everything, each event's payload included). -v still shows the turn narrating itself.
Run an iteration's tool calls concurrently; ordered batches race (provenance P-2).
Directories searched for predictor params; derived from the working dir when unset.
Turns of the CALLER's conversation a subagent is shown. 0 (the default) hands it nothing but its question and :agent-context; an agent that needs the trail asks for it in its own spec (RFC-018).

items.whyNot: :path-permission? is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: Check the paths a tool is given against :allowed-dirs, asking or refusing when they fall outside.

items.whyNot: :permission-mode is a permission key and is never written from inside a turn (RFC-012). A config file outlives the session, so this would widen the gate permanently. Edit .brainyard/config.edn by hand, or pass the flag for this run.
items.doc: :auto-approve | :ask-each-time | :deny-by-default | :auto (approve in a container; else, where a gate would ask, the auto-mode classifier decides and asks only when unsure).
Save the session after every turn under .brainyard/sessions (RFC-016).

Say that a predictor has enough prediction records to compile, once per session, when the pool across sessions reaches this. 150 because the split is 60/20/20: brainyard measured its null on TWELVE val examples, 150 is the first pool whose val split (~30) is not the size already known to fail (RFC-021, byj-gly.57).
Directories searched for predictor specs; derived from the working dir when unset.

Register profile$edit, which changes the project's profile (.brainyard/profile.edn) as the person asks, on their yes, asked every time (RFC-073, byj-8b3). false leaves the profile to /init and the person.
Offer program$* — measure a predictor on a dataset and propose demos. Accepting a proposal stays a CLI action.

items.whyNot: :project-dir belongs to a single run, not to a config file — the CLI and the environment set it. Persisting it would give two answers to where this run is.
items.doc: Root of the project: where .brainyard/ lives. Unset means the git root above the working dir, else the working dir (BY_PROJECT_DIR overrides).

The project's instruction files put in every turn's prompt under ## Project Instructions, in this order — brainyard's :reference-artifact-paths, renamed to match :user-instruction-paths; AGENTS.md first here, where brainyard lists CLAUDE.md first. Resolved against the project dir then the working dir; one reached two ways (a CLAUDE.md that is @AGENTS.md, a symlink) is shown once. [] turns it off (RFC-040).

How many characters of the project's instruction files (:project-instruction-paths) a prompt carries, across all of them, in order — Codex's 32 KiB. A file past what is left is cut at its last heading before the limit, with where the rest is (RFC-040).
Routing key for OpenAI's automatic prefix cache.
Mark the stable prompt zones for provider caching (anthropic; RFC-015).
At startup, remove session and transcript directories past the keep/TTL limits (RFC-016).
Measure again every nth iteration.
How long a turn must run before it earns a recap. A short turn is its own recap; 0 recaps every turn.
Recap every Nth turn of the session (turn N, 2N, …) however short it was, as well as any turn longer than :recap-after-ms; 0 turns it off.
After a long turn, write a two-line recap of where the work stands and what is next (the session/recap predictor).
As a session or a question starts, record the project in ~/.brainyard/projects, the registry by keeps too (RFC-074); a loop evaluation's clones are not recorded.

items.whyNot: :resume belongs to a single run, not to a config file — the CLI and the environment set it. Persisting it would give two answers to where this run is.
items.doc: Session id to continue; the CLI sets it from --resume.
Entries the full-screen renderer keeps to scroll back through, per transcript (the root's and each subagent's). The oldest fall off the top.
How long the session's end waits for self-improvement judges still running before it cancels them — brainyard's await-background-jobs! grace. The call is paid for; its result is worth a short wait.

items.whyNot: :session-id belongs to a single run, not to a config file — the CLI and the environment set it. Persisting it would give two answers to where this run is.
items.doc: Names this run's spill directory under .brainyard/transcripts. Generated per run when unset; two runs in one project must not share it.
Offer session$list, session$status, session$ask, session$send and session$cancel: this project's other live sessions, asked over their session channel (RFC-031).
Sessions older than this may be pruned once beyond the keep count.
The session turn a subagent was dispatched in (set by a dispatch; recorded in its trajectory as :turn, byj-pzb).
How long the person has to allow a turn a coach injected into a shared session; no answer is a refusal (RFC-043).
A session started with --share link is recorded: what it shares is kept and uploaded for review when the share ends, and everyone watching is told. Never a class share (RFC-043).
The relay the share sidecar connects out to, handed to it as its relay (RFC-043); unset, the one byj-share is logged in to, else the sidecar's own default.
The share sidecar a session started with --share runs: a command found on PATH, or a path to one (RFC-043).

The session's agent can share: share$status, share$ls, share$start and share$control, the operations /share runs (RFC-043, byj-gly.362.2). share$start publishes what it shares, so :tool-ask-effects asks before it by default. Never a subagent's.
Offer skills$write and skills$reload (RFC-017).

The most turns a distillation window waits: it is judged as soon as it shows a procedure (a tool sequence repeated, or one long one), and at the latest every N turns; 1 judges each candidate turn as it ends. Whatever is left is judged when the session ends.
The score (0..1) a distilled skill must reach to be staged.
How much of a skill's description its one line in the prompt carries, when its title is only its name — the first sentence, clipped (byj-gly.336).
Directories to load skills from, replacing the defaults (project, ~/.brainyard, ~/.claude, ~/.agents).
Load SKILL.md procedures from .brainyard/skills, ~/.claude/skills and friends (RFC-017).
Read the reply as it is generated, emitting :agent.llm/chunk. Only the claude-code provider can: jolt's http client buffers a whole response before handing it over (RFC-006).
Iteration ceiling for a child turn, unless its agent sets one.
Child turns (dispatches and follow-up asks) one session may spend.
Offer the agent roster from .brainyard/agents and the built-in one.
Park a turn that keeps polling a running task, and tell the agent when a task it left running finishes (RFC-019).
Task directories kept, whatever their age.
Task directories older than this may be pruned.
Default deadline for a task$run job.
Offer task$* and let a slow tool call detach into a background task.
How long team$close waits for a member to close itself before stopping its process.
The command that starts a member session (--serve and its flags are appended). Default: `jolt run:byj` from a checkout, `byj run` from a binary.
How long a member waits for its leader's person to answer a forwarded permission prompt before it counts as a refusal.
How long team$spawn waits for a member to come up.
Offer team$create, team$spawn, team$assign, team$status and team$close: a team of live member sessions this one leads (RFC-032). A member is started with it off.

The session's agent works the Terminal view's programs: terminal$list, terminal$start, terminal$stop, terminal$send and terminal$capture (byj-gly.417), and terminal$context, what the person is looking at in a running editor (byj-gly.453). Offered where tmux is; this project's programs alone. terminal$send types into one, so :tool-ask-effects asks before it by default. Never a subagent's.
The checklist a run continues instead of planning a new one (loops/plan-act-eval.edn).
Offer todo$* — a checklist under .brainyard/todos that survives the turn that wrote it.

The default asks before a share is started (:share/publish: share$start, byj-gly.362.2), before typing into a terminal program (:terminal/input: terminal$send, byj-gly.417, which in a shell runs commands) and before code is run in the person's Emacs (:editor/eval: emacs$eval; :editor/execute: emacs$org-execute, RFC-067); a set given here replaces it, so keep those in it to go on being asked.

Offer list-tools, get-tool-info and search.
The score (0..1) a distilled tool must reach to be proved and staged.
Overrides for Tool Lisp's {:steps :tool-calls} budget.

Tool Lisp extensions in force (byj-gly.258, RFC-010): vocabulary (fnil, compare, key/val, clojure.set/walk/edn, data/diff …), forms (for, doseq, case, cond-> …), control (loop/recur, try/catch/throw, letfn). All three by default; [] is the base language. reach (bounded pmap, now/now-ms, and the store$get/put/keys tools for state between calls — byj-gly.261) is off by default: measured to help where it is wanted (byj-gly.278), and to cost haiku creates and time on the tasks that do not want it (byj-gly.279, byj-gly.293). Add :reach to take it.
Cap on a tool result inside a Tool Lisp body, which no model reads: :max-output-chars is for the prompt.
tool$create and tool$validate rebuild the closers of a body that does not balance from its indentation, when that reads, and say so (byj-gly.260). Off: such a body is refused.

In the prompt, list the primitives and your own tools a line each and every other family (config$, task$, each MCP server …) as one line of names; get-tool-info and list-tools :family give the rest. Off: a line per tool. Needs :compact-agent-tools.
Offer tool$run, one-off Tool Lisp composition.
Append one record per turn to .brainyard/sessions/<id>/trajectory.edn: what the turn did, and what it cost (RFC-025).
Lines of the session's own transcript kept — what /capture writes and a resumed session draws again. The oldest go first; the turns themselves are in the snapshot and the trajectory.
Once a day, look for a newer release of :update-source in the background and say so as a run ends; nothing is installed (byj update does that). Kept in ~/.brainyard/update-check.edn (RFC-029).

The GitHub repo (owner/name) whose newest release `byj update` installs: the public tap's copy of each release, read with no token (byj-gly.181.10). A private repo needs one: GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN, or `gh auth token` (RFC-029).

The person's own instruction files, for every project, under ## User Instructions after the project's — ~/.brainyard/AGENTS.md, which replaces brainyard's ~/.brainyard/BRAINYARD.md. Add ~/.claude/CLAUDE.md or ~/.codex/AGENTS.md to share another tool's; relative paths are against home. [] turns it off (RFC-040).
How many characters of the person's own instruction files a prompt carries: a budget of their own, so a project's never pushes them out.
Load user tools from .brainyard/tools.
Tool-name globs a turn may see. Empty means everything.
